title: A First Course in Abstract Algebra
author: John B. Fraleigh
summary: Undergraduate introduction to groups, rings, fields and Galois theory; one of the most widely used first texts in abstract algebra, valued for its gentle pace and many exercises.

title: A Text Book of Mathematics for II Year Pre-University Course
author: B. G. Umarani & P. G. Umarani
summary: Karnataka second-year PUC mathematics textbook covering the state syllabus (algebra, calculus, coordinate geometry and related topics); a regional exam-preparation text with little published review coverage.

title: Algorithm Design
author: Jon Kleinberg & Éva Tardos
summary: Algorithms textbook organized around design techniques (greedy, divide and conquer, dynamic programming, network flow, NP-completeness, approximation); praised for motivating each technique through real problems.

title: Bayesian Data Analysis
author: Andrew Gelman, John B. Carlin, Hal S. Stern, Donald B. Rubin
summary: The standard reference on applied Bayesian statistics, covering hierarchical models, model checking and computation (MCMC); widely used as a graduate text.

title: Computational Mathematics
summary: A textbook on computational mathematics (numerical methods and computation-oriented mathematics); the specific author and edition could not be identified from the photo.

title: Computer Networks
summary: A general textbook on computer networks (protocol layers, the Internet stack, routing and transport); the specific author and edition could not be identified from the photo.

title: DSL Illuminated
summary: A technical book on DSL; the author, edition and even whether it concerns Digital Subscriber Line networking or domain-specific languages could not be confirmed from available sources.

title: Deep Learning
author: Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, Aaron Courville
summary: Comprehensive MIT Press text covering the mathematical background, modern practice and research frontiers of deep neural networks; long regarded as the field's standard reference.

title: Deliberate Practice in Discrete Mathematics
summary: A practice-oriented discrete mathematics workbook; author and publication details could not be confirmed and little published review coverage exists.

title: Discrete Mathematics
author: Norman L. Biggs
summary: Oxford introductory text covering logic, counting, graphs, algorithms and algebraic structures; respected for its rigor and clarity at the undergraduate level.

title: Elements of ML Programming
author: Jeffrey D. Ullman
summary: Introduction to programming in Standard ML (ML97 in later editions), covering types, pattern matching, higher-order functions and modules; a well-known teaching text for SML.

title: Learn Physics with Functional Programming
author: Scott N. Walck
summary: No Starch Press book teaching Haskell through Newtonian mechanics and electromagnetism simulations; noted for treating physics as code with types.

title: Machine Learning
summary: A general machine learning textbook; the specific author and edition could not be identified from the photo.

title: Operating System Principles
author: Abraham Silberschatz, Peter B. Galvin, Greg Gagne
summary: Edition of the long-running 'dinosaur book' on processes, scheduling, memory, file systems and protection; one of the most widely adopted OS textbooks.

title: Probability, Random Variables, and Stochastic Processes
author: Athanasios Papoulis
summary: Classic engineering-oriented text on probability theory and random processes; a standard reference in electrical engineering and signal processing for decades.

title: Programming Language Pragmatics
author: Michael L. Scott
summary: Broad survey of language design and implementation, linking syntax, semantics and compilation across many paradigms; a common text for comparative programming languages courses.

title: Satan, Cantor and Infinity
author: Raymond M. Smullyan
summary: Collection of logic puzzles (knights and knaves and beyond) that build up to Cantor's ideas about infinity; typical of Smullyan's playful route into serious logic.

title: Software Engineering Basics
summary: An introductory software engineering text; the specific author and edition could not be identified from the photo.

title: The Kodansha Kanji Learner's Course
author: Andrew Scott Conning
summary: Sequenced course covering 2,300 kanji with mnemonics and example vocabulary, ordered so components appear before the characters that use them; well regarded among self-learners.

title: Type-Driven Development with Idris
author: Edwin Brady
summary: Manning book by Idris's creator showing how dependent types can guide program construction; an accessible practical introduction to dependently typed programming.

title: UNIX Network Programming
author: W. Richard Stevens
summary: The definitive guide to sockets and inter-process communication programming on Unix; long treated as the canonical reference for network programmers.

title: Learning Concurrent Programming in Scala
author: Aleksandar Prokopec
summary: Packt book covering the JVM memory model, futures and promises, parallel collections, reactive extensions, STM and actors in Scala; written by a Scala parallel collections author.

title: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide, Volume 2
author: Alex Xu & Sahn Lam
summary: Diagram-heavy walkthroughs of large-scale system design problems (proximity services, payment systems, stock exchanges and more); popular interview-preparation sequel.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms
author: Alfred V. Aho, John E. Hopcroft, Jeffrey D. Ullman
summary: Classic Addison-Wesley text on abstract data types, sorting, searching, graphs and algorithm analysis, presented with Pascal; a foundational undergraduate reference.

title: Category Theory for Programmers
author: Bartosz Milewski
summary: Book version of Milewski's blog series explaining categories, functors, monads, adjunctions and more with Haskell and C++ examples; a popular entry point for programmers.

title: Types and Programming Languages
author: Benjamin C. Pierce
summary: The standard graduate text on type systems, from the untyped lambda calculus through subtyping, recursive types and polymorphism, with OCaml implementations.

title: The C++ Programming Language
author: Bjarne Stroustrup
summary: The language's creator's comprehensive reference and tutorial, revised across editions to track the C++ standards; the authoritative book on C++.

title: The C Programming Language
author: Brian W. Kernighan, Dennis M. Ritchie
summary: 'K&R', the concise original description of C by its co-designer; celebrated as a model of clear technical writing.

title: Real World Haskell
author: Bryan O'Sullivan, John Goerzen & Don Stewart
summary: O'Reilly book applying Haskell to practical tasks (I/O, parsing, databases, concurrency, testing); influential in bringing Haskell to working programmers, though parts are now dated.

title: Elements of Discrete Mathematics
author: C. L. Liu
summary: McGraw-Hill computer-science-oriented discrete mathematics text covering sets, combinatorics, graphs, recurrences and algebraic systems; a long-standing course text, especially in India.

title: Purely Functional Data Structures
author: Chris Okasaki
summary: Expanded from Okasaki's thesis, it shows how to design and analyze efficient immutable data structures using laziness and amortization; the classic work on the subject.

title: The Dialogues: Conversations about the Nature of the Universe
author: Clifford V. Johnson
summary: Graphic novel by a theoretical physicist in which pairs of characters discuss cosmology, quantum mechanics and other physics ideas; praised as an inventive work of science communication.

title: How to Prove It: A Structured Approach
author: Daniel J. Velleman
summary: Introduction to logic, sets and proof techniques for students moving into abstract mathematics; a widely recommended transition-to-proofs text.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
summary: Nobel laureate's popular account of the two-systems model of thought and research on heuristics and biases; a bestseller, though some of the priming studies it cites have since failed to replicate.

title: The Little Learner: A Straight Line to Deep Learning
author: Daniel P. Friedman & Anurag Mendhekar
summary: MIT Press book in the 'Little' question-and-answer style that builds deep learning concepts from scratch in a Scheme dialect.

title: Iai: The Art of Drawing the Sword
author: Darrell Max Craig
summary: Tuttle manual on Japanese iaido covering etiquette, equipment and solo sword-drawing forms; an early English-language introduction with little published criticism.

title: Computer Organization and Design: The Hardware/Software Interface
author: David A. Patterson and John L. Hennessy
summary: The standard undergraduate text on processor design, the memory hierarchy and the hardware/software boundary, by the Turing Award-winning RISC pioneers.

title: Parallel Computer Architecture: A Hardware/Software Approach
author: David E. Culler, Jaswinder Pal Singh, Anoop Gupta
summary: Graduate text on multiprocessor design, cache coherence, interconnects and parallel program workloads; a classic reference for parallel architecture.

title: DSLs in Action
author: Debasish Ghosh
summary: Manning book on designing internal and external domain-specific languages in Scala, Groovy, Ruby and Clojure, with financial-domain examples.

title: Functional and Reactive Domain Modeling
author: Debasish Ghosh
summary: Manning book applying algebraic, functional and reactive techniques to domain-driven design in Scala; noted for linking DDD with functional abstractions.

title: Drawing Physics: 2,600 Years of Discovery from Thales to Higgs
author: Don S. Lemons
summary: MIT Press survey of 51 key ideas in physics, each explained with a hand-drawn illustration and a short essay; well received as an accessible history.

title: The Art of Computer Programming, Volume 3: Sorting and Searching
author: Donald E. Knuth
summary: Knuth's exhaustive mathematical treatment of sorting and searching algorithms; part of the series widely considered the definitive work on algorithm analysis.

title: Internetworking with TCP/IP, Volume II: Design, Implementation, and Internals
author: Douglas E. Comer, David L. Stevens
summary: Walks through the code of a working TCP/IP implementation, covering IP, ICMP, UDP, TCP and routing internals; a classic companion to Comer's protocol volume.

title: Internetworking with TCP/IP, Volume III: Client-Server Programming and Applications
author: Douglas E. Comer, David L. Stevens
summary: Covers designing and implementing client-server network applications over sockets; part of Comer's well-regarded TCP/IP series.

title: Wing Chun Kung-Fu: A Complete Guide, Volume 1 – Basic Forms and Principles
author: Dr. Joseph Wayne Smith
summary: Tuttle manual presenting Wing Chun's foundational forms and principles with photo sequences; little published criticism exists.

title: Wing Chun Kung-Fu: A Complete Guide, Volume 2 – Fighting and Grappling
author: Dr. Joseph Wayne Smith
summary: Companion volume covering Wing Chun fighting applications and grappling techniques; little published criticism exists.

title: Comprehensive Asian Fighting Arts
author: Donn F. Draeger & Robert W. Smith
summary: Survey of fighting arts across Asia by two pioneering Western martial arts scholars; long valued as a reference, though later research has revised some historical claims.

title: Category Theory in Context
author: Emily Riehl
summary: Dover graduate introduction covering categories, universal properties, the Yoneda lemma, limits, adjunctions and monads, with examples drawn from across mathematics; freely available and widely recommended.

title: Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software
author: Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides
summary: The 'Gang of Four' catalog of 23 object-oriented design patterns; hugely influential on software design vocabulary, though critics note several patterns compensate for missing language features.

title: ZooKeeper: Distributed Process Coordination
author: Flavio Junqueira & Benjamin Reed
summary: O'Reilly guide by two of ZooKeeper's creators to using and operating it for coordination tasks such as leader election, locks and configuration.

title: How to Solve It
author: G. Pólya
summary: Classic short book on mathematical problem-solving heuristics (understand, plan, carry out, look back); among the most influential works on mathematical thinking.

title: Understanding Kanji Characters by Their Ancestral Forms
author: Ping-gam Go
summary: Explains kanji through their ancient pictographic and seal-script origins; the kanji edition of the author's book on Chinese characters, with limited critical coverage.

title: Cracking the Coding Interview
author: Gayle Laakmann McDowell
summary: Best-selling preparation guide with 189 programming problems and solutions plus advice on technical interviews at large tech companies.

title: Distributed Systems: Concepts and Design
author: George Coulouris, Jean Dollimore, Tim Kindberg
summary: Long-running textbook on distributed system models, communication, naming, time, coordination, replication and transactions; a standard course text.

title: Becoming a Technical Leader: An Organic Problem-Solving Approach
author: Gerald M. Weinberg
summary: Weinberg's guide to leadership for technical people, built around motivation, organization and innovation; regarded as a classic of software management writing.

title: Analysis of Genuine Karate: Misconceptions, Origins, Development, and True Purpose
author: Hermann Bayer
summary: YMAA book examining karate kata, bunkai and history to argue for the art's original self-defense purpose; followed by a second volume, with little published criticism.

title: High Performance Spark
author: Holden Karau & Rachel Warren
summary: O'Reilly guide to tuning and scaling Apache Spark jobs (partitioning, joins, memory, Datasets) with Scala examples.

title: Linkers and Loaders
author: John R. Levine
summary: The best-known book devoted to linking, loading, object file formats, relocation and shared libraries; still a go-to reference on the subject.

title: Principles of Digital Communication
author: J. Das, S. K. Mullick, P. K. Chatterjee
summary: Indian engineering textbook (Wiley Eastern / New Age) on signal representation, detection and estimation for digital communication; a standard text in Indian EE curricula.

title: A Life Decoded: My Genome: My Life
author: J. Craig Venter
summary: Venter's memoir of his career and the race to sequence the human genome; reviewers found it vivid but self-promoting.

title: Life at the Speed of Light: From the Double Helix to the Dawn of Digital Life
author: J. Craig Venter
summary: Popular-science account of synthetic biology and his team's creation of a cell with a synthetic genome; praised for its subject, though critics noted its self-congratulatory tone.

title: Intel Threading Building Blocks
author: James Reinders
summary: O'Reilly guide to Intel's C++ TBB library for task-based multicore parallelism, covering parallel algorithms, containers and the task scheduler.

title: Remembering the Kanji
author: James W. Heisig
summary: Mnemonic method for learning the meanings and writing of the jōyō kanji through stories built from components; very popular, though critics note it defers readings and vocabulary.

title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning
author: Gareth James, Daniela Witten, Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani
summary: Accessible introduction to regression, classification, resampling, trees, SVMs and unsupervised learning with R (later Python) labs; a widely used free textbook.

title: The Boost Graph Library: User Guide and Reference Manual
author: Jeremy G. Siek, Lie-Quan Lee, Andrew Lumsdaine
summary: Guide and reference for the generic C++ BGL, demonstrating generic programming applied to graph algorithms.

title: A Programmer's Introduction to Mathematics
author: Jeremy Kun
summary: Self-published introduction to proofs, sets, graphs, calculus, linear algebra and more, aimed at programmers and paired with code applications; well received by its target readers.

title: The Abacus: A Pocket Computer
author: Jesse Dilson
summary: Short St. Martin's Press book on the history of the abacus and how to calculate with it, later reissued as 'The Abacus: The World's First Computing System'.

title: Computer Networks: A Systems Approach
author: Larry L. Peterson, Bruce S. Davie
summary: Networking textbook emphasizing the design principles behind real systems and protocols; a standard alternative to layer-by-layer texts and now freely available online.

title: Electromagnetics
author: John D. Kraus
summary: Classic engineering electromagnetics text covering static fields, Maxwell's equations, waves, transmission lines and antennas, by the noted antenna pioneer.

title: Introduction to Automata Theory, Languages, and Computation
author: John E. Hopcroft, Rajeev Motwani, Jeffrey D. Ullman
summary: The 'Cinderella book', a standard text on finite automata, grammars, Turing machines, decidability and complexity; later editions with Motwani made it more accessible.

title: Computer Architecture: A Quantitative Approach
author: John L. Hennessy, David A. Patterson
summary: The graduate standard on processor and memory design, driven by quantitative performance analysis; credited with shaping how architecture is taught.

title: Graph Theory with Applications to Engineering and Computer Science
author: Narsingh Deo
summary: Prentice-Hall text on graph theory with applications to networks, coding and algorithms; a staple of Indian engineering curricula.

title: The Modern English-Nihongo Dictionary (日本語学習英日辞典)
author: Nihongo Gakushū Ei-Nichi Jiten editorial committee
summary: English-to-Japanese learner's dictionary designed for non-native students of Japanese, with example sentences and usage notes; little published review coverage.

title: Randomized Algorithms
author: Rajeev Motwani & Prabhakar Raghavan
summary: The standard reference on randomized algorithm design and probabilistic analysis, covering tail bounds, Markov chains and applications across computing.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
summary: O'Reilly survey of the principles behind databases, replication, partitioning, transactions, consistency and stream processing; widely regarded as the go-to book on modern data systems.

title: Scala for Machine Learning
author: Patrick R. Nicolas
summary: Packt book implementing classic machine learning algorithms (regression, clustering, Markov models, SVMs, neural networks) in Scala.

title: Functional Programming in Scala
author: Paul Chiusano & Rúnar Bjarnason
summary: The 'red book': an exercise-driven course in deriving functional abstractions (monoids, monads, applicatives, streams) from first principles; considered a classic of FP pedagogy.

title: The Haskell School of Music: From Signals to Symphonies
author: Paul Hudak, Donya Quick
summary: Cambridge book teaching Haskell through computer music using the Euterpea library, covering algorithmic composition and signal processing.

title: First-Order Logic
author: Raymond M. Smullyan
summary: Concise monograph that popularized analytic tableaux as a proof method for first-order logic; admired for its elegance and still in print from Dover.

title: The Gödelian Puzzle Book: Puzzles, Paradoxes and Proofs
author: Raymond M. Smullyan
summary: Dover collection of logic puzzles leading readers toward Gödel's incompleteness theorems, written in Smullyan's characteristic playful style.

title: What Is the Name of This Book?
author: Raymond M. Smullyan
summary: Smullyan's best-known puzzle book, introducing knights-and-knaves puzzles and building to Gödel's incompleteness ideas; a classic of recreational logic.

title: Set Theory and the Continuum Problem
author: Raymond M. Smullyan and Melvin Fitting
summary: Graduate text on axiomatic set theory leading to the independence of the continuum hypothesis via constructibility and forcing; praised for its clear, unified treatment.

title: Pearls of Functional Algorithm Design
author: Richard Bird
summary: Thirty short chapters deriving efficient Haskell algorithms through equational reasoning; a celebrated showcase of program calculation.

title: Pattern Classification
author: Richard O. Duda, Peter E. Hart, David G. Stork
summary: Classic text on statistical pattern recognition (Bayesian decision theory, parametric and nonparametric methods, neural networks, clustering); the 2001 second edition added Stork.

title: Crafting Interpreters
author: Robert Nystrom
summary: Hands-on book building a tree-walking interpreter in Java and a bytecode VM in C for the Lox language; widely praised for its clarity and illustrations.
